sections.title: Core Concept
sections.content: Level 2 Data Interpretation tables contain larger datasets with multiple categories such as year-wise sales, product-wise revenue, or region-wise performance. Questions involve percentage change, profit calculation, averages, and comparisons between categories.

sections.title: ₹ Based Example
sections.content: Suppose a table shows sales and expenses of 4 products in ₹ for 3 years. You may need to calculate profit for each year, percentage growth from one year to another, or find which product contributed the highest total revenue.

sections.title: Important Formulas
sections.content:
1. Profit = Sales - Expense
2. Profit % = (Profit / Expense) × 100
3. Percentage Change = (New - Old) / Old × 100
4. Average = Total ÷ Number of values

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Taking wrong base value while calculating percentage change
2. Mixing total and average values
3. Ignoring units like ₹ in thousands or lakhs
4. Not reading year or category labels carefully

sections.title: Smart Strategy
sections.content:
1. Identify whether the question needs total, percentage, or comparison
2. Calculate totals first if multiple values are involved
3. Use approximation when options are far apart
4. Avoid lengthy calculations if ratio comparison works

tricks.title: 10% Anchor Method
tricks.explanation: First find 10%, then build other percentages from it.

tricks.title: Successive Change Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If increase by a% and then b%, net change = a + b + (ab/100).

tricks.title: Reverse Percentage Method
tricks.explanation: If value after 25% increase is given, multiply by 100/125 to get original.

tricks.title: Ratio Comparison Trick
tricks.explanation: Instead of converting to percentage, compare by cross multiplication.

tricks.title: Average Adjustment Trick
tricks.explanation: If one value is replaced, adjust average using difference method.
tricks.example: If ₹500 replaces ₹400 in 5 items, total increases by ₹100

tricks.title: Profit Comparison Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Compare profit directly instead of profit percentage if base costs are same.

tricks.title: Approximation Strategy
tricks.explanation: Round numbers for quick calculation when exact value is not required.
tricks.example: ₹498 can be treated as ₹500 for fast mental math

tricks.title: Quick Growth Check
tricks.explanation: Check difference first, then calculate percentage only if needed.
